newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Poor SAS figures flag arrival of tougher times.
newsitem.headline: Poor SAS figures flag arrival of tougher times.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines Systems (SAS) Monday reported a 31 percent slump in 1996 profits and warned that competition was likely to get even tougher in Scandinavian skies in 1997.
The airline, owned by the governments of Denmark, Norway and Sweden and private investors, reported a pre-tax profit of 1.82 billion crowns ($246 million) for 1996.
The profit was above a company forecast of 1.74 billion crowns ($235 million) made in mid-November and above an average market prediction of 1.72 billion crowns ($232 million).
